newsitem.title: GERMANY: Foreign buying of German securities jumped in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying of German securities jumped in Nov.

text.p: Germany enjoyed a net inflow of 18.8 billion marks worth of capital from abroad in November as foreign investors bought domestic German securities, especially bonds, the Bundesbank said on Tuesday.
The inflow compared with a net outflow of 0.8 billion marks on October.
Foreign investors in November bought a net 21.9 billion marks worth of German securities, with bonds accounting for the lion's share with 21.1 billion marks.
Foreign demand was concentrated on public sector bonds, net purchases of which totalled 15.4 billion marks.
Net purchases of equities by foreigners totalled 4.7 billion marks in November, contrasting with net sales totalling 0.7 billion marks in October.
The swing was explained by foreign buying of Deutsche Telekom AG shares which were floated in November, the Bundesbank said.
The securities purchases contrast with net foreign sales of 4.9 billion marks worth of domestic financial derivatives in November, the Bundesbank said.
Meanwhile German net investment in foreign securities fell to 3.1 billion marks in October from 4.5 billion marks in October.
